Five call sites produce the five members, and they split across TWO binding classes: platinum_cli.py:66 gc.cached('platinum.routing', ...) and :87 gc.cached('platinum.dataflows', ...) are CLASS 1 -- call-site string literals. platinum_cli.py:80 gc.cached(f'platinum.dag.{firm}', ...) is CLASS 2 -- the name is INTERPOLATED, but from an allow-list, not from arbitrary input: :146 resolves firm = FIRM_ALIAS.get((args.firm or 'bd').lower(), 'bd'), so an unrecognised --firm falls back to 'bd' rather than flowing into the cache name.

declared_opinions: A STAT-ONLY FINGERPRINT IS GOOD ENOUGH FOR A CACHE (:190). The module implements BOTH a stat-only source_fingerprint (:142-167, max-mtime + file count) and a checkout-invariant content_fingerprint (:170-198, sha256 over content), and DELIBERATELY gives the caches the stat-only one for cost. :153 records the consequence in the module's own words -- a checkout 're-stamps every mtime BY CONSTRUCTION on a content-identical tree' -- so the cheap signal manufactures staleness. A declared cost/correctness trade, not a derived result.

DEFAULT IS HEAD-PINNED (:261-266). A within-TTL cache whose fingerprint has drifted is a MISS rather than a serve. The comment records this as a joint verdict of 2026-07-01 that killed the stale-cache-phantom class, and explicitly extended fingerprint-honouring from FRESH to DEFAULT.

A UNUSABLE CACHE SHOULD REBUILD SILENTLY (:251-257). Every failure to load -- corrupt pickle, protocol mismatch, wrong payload type -- returns (None, None), identical to a cache that does not exist. Treating corruption as absence is a choice; it is safe for correctness and silent for diagnosis.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: SILENTLY REBUILDS, IN EVERY FAILURE DIRECTION. load() returns (None, None) -- indistinguishable from 'no cache exists' -- when the file is absent (:249-250), when unpickling raises ANY exception (:251-255, a bare `except Exception`), when the payload is not a CachePayload (:256-257), when age >= ttl (:259-260), and when the fingerprint has drifted (:265-266). cached() then calls the builder and overwrites. Nothing is logged and nothing is raised, so a corrupt cache, a stale cache and an absent cache produce identical observable behaviour: a slower call.
silent_degrade_paths: ⛔ THE ONE THAT HAS ALREADY COST THIS ESTATE A NUMBER: the TTL gates load() ONLY. Anything that opens a .cache file directly and unpickles it bypasses every freshness check in this module -- no TTL, no fingerprint, no age. And that is not hypothetical here: org/projects/NFRA_GRAPHUNI/NFRA_GRAPHUNI.P0-A.storage-stratum-audit.md records platinum.dag.inf.cache as STALE with s3_keys=0 while its bd and cot siblings held 103 and 96, and the F2 finding warns in terms 'do not let a stale-cache 0 understate the inf storage denominator.' A stale member of THIS family, read outside the API that would have rejected it, produced a zero that read as a measurement.

The bare `except Exception` at :251-255 turns instrument failure into a verdict: a genuinely corrupt or truncated pickle is reported as 'no cache', so corruption never surfaces and the file is simply overwritten on the next call. Safe for correctness, invisible for diagnosis.

The stat-only fingerprint (:142-167) is deliberately preferred over the content fingerprint (:170-198), and :153 records that a checkout re-stamps every mtime on a content-identical tree. That manufactures staleness -- a FALSE MISS, which costs a rebuild and never a wrong answer. I record the direction explicitly because the same module contains the instrument that would not have this failure, and choosing the cheaper one was deliberate.

built_at is the WRITE time, not the vintage of the source the object was built from. A consumer reading built_at as 'the data is this fresh' is reading when the cache was written, not what it was written from; source vintage lives in the fingerprint, which is opaque and is compared, never displayed.
cache_file() constructs a path for any string with no validation, so the family's enumerability depends entirely on discipline at five call sites rather than on any guard.

I did not construct that scenario -- I found the estate had already run it. ⚠ AND IT RESOLVES AN APPARENT CONTRADICTION ON THIS CARD, which is why I chased it rather than citing both facts side by side: if every read through load() is a guaranteed MISS (cadence row), a stale cache should be unable to harm anyone. The incident proves harm occurred. Both are true because the harm came through a DIRECT read, outside the API -- so the TTL protects the API's callers and protects nobody else. A card carrying both facts without reconciling them would have looked complete and been incoherent.

verdict.why: The family is well-built and precisely bounded, and it is the rare subject where coverage can be CLOSED rather than merely sampled: the complete name space is derivable from the producer -- two call-site literals plus a token normalised through a three-value allow-list with a default -- so 5 declared, 5 derivable, 5 present and 0 undeclared is a closed population verified by two independent instruments, code and filesystem. Writes are atomic via os.replace, DEFAULT is head-pinned against fingerprint drift, and the module implements and documents both a cheap and a rigorous staleness signal. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on three measured defects: (1) EVERY MEMBER IS 3 TO 36 DAYS OLD AGAINST A 300-SECOND TTL, so load()'s age branch is taken on every read for every member -- these five present, non-empty files cannot be served through the API that wrote them, and every invocation rebuilds; (2) the TTL and fingerprint gate load() ONLY, and a direct unpickle bypasses both -- not hypothetically, since the NFRA_GRAPHUNI P0-A audit records a stale member of this exact family producing an s3_keys=0 that had to be explicitly warned against as a denominator; (3) every failure direction -- absent, corrupt, wrong type, expired, drifted -- returns the identical (None, None), so corruption is indistinguishable from absence and never surfaces. Not UNSOUND: nothing measured shows a wrong value served THROUGH the API, and every defect above degrades toward rebuilding rather than toward a false answer. NOT INCOMPLETE: all 7 rows worked, every scalar measured. ⛔ NO COMPLETENESS CLAIM about writers of .comp-graph generally -- this card closes its own part id and nothing wider. ⛔ NO FORWARD DISPOSITION: the TTL evidence invites a retire-or-refresh opinion and that is exactly the second-pass judgement a carding lane must not make about its own subject. Per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX this lane touched no cache, ran no comp-platinum invocation (which would have rewritten members and destroyed the age evidence), and committed nothing to graph_cache.py or platinum_cli.py.
blocking_defects: For anyone assuming comp-platinum is served from cache: it is not. All five members exceed the 300s TTL by three to thirty-six days, so every read misses and every invocation rebuilds. The caches are residue, not a warm path. Owner 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp.
